_about: Creative scores, 1 to 10, on the rubric in src/rubric.md. Qualitative judgement from looking at the posted PNGs at phone width (360 px tiles), not a measurement: never cite a score as evidence that something performs. worked / failed / fix are about the creative; performance verdicts come from the export (performance-ranking.csv).

2026-10-07-new-sibling.worked: A topic that sells (the two new sibling titles together have 132 orders, fourth of all books, in docs/lumebook-sales-data-decisions-2026-10-12.md), one warm family across all slides, big headlines that read easily on a phone.
2026-10-07-new-sibling.failed: The cover promises 5 things to notice, but the slides are unnumbered reassurances with no action to take. Two CTAs: the caption asks for comments, the slide sends to the bio link, and the bio link cannot be traced to the post. Slide 7 (אל תחכו לרגע שבו הכול משתנה) leans on urgency.
2026-10-07-new-sibling.fix: Number the five items and give each one a small action; end with one CTA (the code word and a tagged DM link).

2026-10-08-gan-dropoff.worked: Child's voice on a sharp real moment (crying at the gate, parents driving to work with it in their head), two concrete tools, open loops that carry each swipe, posted in the first week after the Sukkot break.
2026-10-08-gan-dropoff.failed: The cover shows the child from behind and the parents small in the distance, so nothing in the picture stops the scroll (the face-to-viewer rule came two days later). No organic like, save, share or comment.
2026-10-08-gan-dropoff.fix: Cover with the child's face to the viewer mid-feeling; keep the copy as it is.

2026-10-09-games-attention.worked: Concrete game picks with a how-to tip for each; an honest LumeBook slide that says what the story is about.
2026-10-09-games-attention.failed: The cover says 4 board games, but one of the 4 is the LumeBook book. Small product shots on cream do not stop the scroll. The ending asks for a save and a comment and gives no way to reach the book.
2026-10-09-games-attention.fix: Count only the games in the title (or say 3 games and a book), and end on one CTA to the book.

2026-10-09-books-feelings.worked: Well-known Israeli picture books with a question to ask after each one; the LumeBook book sits naturally among them.
2026-10-09-books-feelings.failed: A category cover with small book covers; the ending asks for a save and a comment and gives no way to reach the book.
2026-10-09-books-feelings.fix: End with one CTA to the feelings book.

2026-10-11-first-grade.worked: The sharpest contrast hook in the set (בכיתה הוא מלאך, בבית הר געש), an exaggerated face to the viewer, highlight blocks that read well at phone size, two practical tools.
2026-10-11-first-grade.failed: Despite the strongest cover, one of the lowest reaches. It went up the same day as two other carousels, so it may have competed with them (a guess, not tested). The audience is narrow: first grade only.
2026-10-11-first-grade.fix: Post one carousel a day; re-run this hook on a quiet day to see whether the low reach was the creative or the crowding.

2026-10-11-books-helping.worked: Classic Israeli books parents know; the LumeBook story about sharing a toy box fits the theme.
2026-10-11-books-helping.failed: Only two outside books plus ours behind a 3 books cover. The LumeBook slide uses a photo-real child, unlike every other LumeBook picture. The slide asks a question while the caption asks for לומי: two CTAs.
2026-10-11-books-helping.fix: Make the last slide and the caption ask for the same one thing.

2026-10-11-games-planning.worked: The highlight on כמה צעדים קדימה names a skill parents want; good picks for age 6 with a question to ask during play.
2026-10-11-games-planning.failed: 4 board games where one is the book; the slide asks a question while the caption asks for לומי.
2026-10-11-games-planning.fix: One CTA, and a title that counts honestly.

2026-10-12-screen-off.worked: The most universal moment in the set, told to the mother with the child's feeling on slide 3, and two sentences a parent can use tonight.
2026-10-12-screen-off.failed: The bridge from screens to a personalised story is vague, so the CTA has little reason behind it. No organic save, share or comment.
2026-10-12-screen-off.fix: Make the story slide say what kind of story helps here (one about finishing something fun), so the CTA follows from the advice.

2026-10-14-sorry.worked: The child pushes back on a sentence every parent says; six numbered alternatives a parent can do; clean text; a clear code-word chip. The best organic response in the export (5 shares, 2 code-word comments).
2026-10-14-sorry.failed: The same picture sits behind all 10 slides, so slides 2 to 9 look the same and only the text changes. The story slide does not say what the book would be about.
2026-10-14-sorry.fix: Keep the format; vary the picture a little per slide (a crop or a prop), and name the story on slide 10.

2026-10-15-elior.worked: The only post that shows the real book in a child's hands, with real joy from a real family. The playbook's market examples found product in use doing better than product alone (docs/lumebook-instagram-carousel-playbook-he.md, section 13.4).
2026-10-15-elior.failed: Slide 3 says the pictures were made בעזרת AI, which breaks the project rule against AI wording in audience copy. Age 10 with special needs is outside the 2 to 8 core. There is no takeaway for a parent who is not buying today. The video stills are soft.
2026-10-15-elior.fix: Next customer story: a child aged 2 to 8 at a known moment (gan, sibling, pacifier), no AI wording, and one line on how the parent made the book.

2026-10-16-words.worked: Seven solid picks split into games and books, each with an age; an honest count.
2026-10-16-words.failed: A category-label cover. The LumeBook slide uses a photo-real child. The slide asks a question while the caption asks for לומי.
2026-10-16-words.fix: The games and books format is stopped since 18 Oct. If it returns: open on a child moment, not a category, and ask for one thing.

2026-10-18-clock-change.worked: Posted a week before the clock change, with the child's question as the hook and six concrete steps.
2026-10-18-clock-change.failed: Dark plum text on a mid-blue picture is the weakest contrast in the set; the body lines are hard to read at phone size. The link to any book is weak.
2026-10-18-clock-change.fix: A lighter area or panel behind the text on blue pictures (or white text).

2026-10-20-pacifier.worked: The pacifier in her mouth tells the topic before any text is read. Its matching book, ביי ביי מוצץ (book 41), has 86 orders, fifth of all books (docs/lumebook-sales-data-decisions-2026-10-12.md). The highest reach and the most organic saves in the export; one parent gave the child's name in the comments.
2026-10-20-pacifier.failed: The same blue contrast problem as the clock change post, and the same picture behind every slide.
2026-10-20-pacifier.fix: Fix the contrast, and send the tagged link to book 41 in the DM.

2026-10-21-potty-accidents.worked: The real reason curiosity is paid off on slide 3; a doctor check and no going back to diapers are practical; the diaper goodbye book has 66 orders in the sales notes.
2026-10-21-potty-accidents.failed: Slide 2 is the densest slide in the set (three lines plus a source). Her eyes look to the side, not at the viewer. Only 3 days old at export.
2026-10-21-potty-accidents.fix: Cut slide 2 to two lines; read it again in the 31 Oct export.

2026-10-23-sibling-fights.worked: A strong angry face to the viewer and a warm scene with the brother in the back; useful, specific tools.
2026-10-23-sibling-fights.failed: Nine items squeezed into six slides (two per slide on three of them). The caption promises a book where your children are the heroes while the slide says your daughter. Less than a day old at export.
2026-10-23-sibling-fights.fix: Six items, one per slide; make the caption match the slide.
